reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every real inner-product space E,every real kappa>=1,and every z=(x,p) in E x E,with Q_kappa(x,p)=(1/(2kappa)+1/2)||x||^2+<x,p>+||p||^2,one has
  Q_kappa(x,p) <= (3/2)(||x||^2+||p||^2).
This is an explicit coordinate-sum energy bound,not a default maximum product norm bound. No completeness,finite-dimensionality or probability condition is imposed.
objects: E,kappa,z=(x,p);real quadratic form Q_kappa and coordinate-sum squared-norm energy.
domains: E is a real inner-product space;kappa in R;z in E x E. Both expressions are real. No measurable,complete or finite-dimensional requirement is stated.
quantifiers: For every real-inner-product E,every kappa>=1 and every phase vector z,the given inequality holds. No existential witness or measure is present.
assumptions: kappa>=1 and the stated E structure;Q_kappa has the approved explicit formula. No added positivity premise,moment or dimension hypothesis occurs.
scopes: This is the upper pointwise energy comparison,with ordinary energy the explicit coordinate sum. It does not separately conclude the opposite comparison or a transport/moment bound. No material ambiguity is present.
constant_dependencies: Exact factor is 3/2,uniform over kappa>=1,z and dimension. Q retains its exact kappa-dependent position coefficient,cross coefficient 1 and momentum coefficient 1.
